text: 🇲🇽✊ "I had practically nothing. I slept on the floor with my children." — Olga Lidia Rodríguez, Vivienda para el Bienestar beneficiary, Lerdo, Durango Olga is a single mother of four who earns the minimum wage and spent six years moving from rental to rental. Today she received her own home in Lerdo, Durango, one of 303 delivered there. The Vivienda para el Bienestar program has now placed 44,000 homes in 27 states, with eight more developments opening in October. In Durango alone, the 25,000-home goal means 15 billion pesos of investment and about 100,000 jobs, according to Governor Esteban Villegas.

🇲🇽✊ "The fundamental rule of the medical model is zero rejections." — Alejandro Svarch, director of IMSS-Bienestar From January 2027, 12,750 primary care clinics will open in the 24 states that joined IMSS-Bienestar. Anyone can walk in, whether they have IMSS, ISSSTE, Pemex or no coverage at all. Care will be free, with 60 basic medicines. Mexico's health system has been fragmented since 1943; this is the first step toward universal service. Neighborhood committees will receive the funds to fix up each site. Since September 14, 73,000 doctors and nurses have applied to staff them, and retired ones can join without losing their pension.

🇲🇽✊ "It is a government that doesn't wait for people to come, but goes out to meet them and knocks on the door of their home." — Leticia Ramírez, Secretary of Well-being Salud Casa por Casa has made more than 27 million free home medical visits to older adults and people with disabilities who receive well-being pensions. Health workers have knocked on 10 million doors, and 8.3 million people have had a second visit. Patients found with uncontrolled hypertension or diabetes are referred to IMSS, ISSSTE, IMSS-Bienestar or Pemex: more than 850,000 for hypertension and 225,000 for diabetes so far. Nurses have handled over 45,000 emergencies.
banner: 27 MILLION FREE DOCTOR VISITS AT HOME

text: 🇲🇽🔍 "They were carrying out an operation on the ground." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 6, 2026 Asked about the CIA's undisclosed operations in Chihuahua, where two US agents died, Sheinbaum said the Attorney General's Office still has the investigation open and has to report its progress. "One must always lament the loss of lives, but they were carrying out an operation on the ground." Any state government that wants a security relationship with a US agency, or any foreign government, has to go through the high-level security group and get authorization from the Foreign Ministry.

text: 🇲🇽🌎 "We want a good relationship with the United States within the framework of our sovereignty, our territorial integrity, mutual trust, and coordination without subordination." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 6, 2026 After US claims that shots were fired at its Coast Guard from Mexico, Washington has sent some of the evidence Mexico requested. Mexico's Defense and Navy ministries are in contact with US Northern Command and the Coast Guard. One "mirror operation" has been carried out and a second is under way, "each in its own territory." If the US government wants a relationship with a Mexican state, Sheinbaum said, it has to go through the Foreign Ministry.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Mexico Sold the US More Than Ever in August: $60.6 Billion</u>

Mexican exports to the United States hit $60.6 billion in August, the highest monthly figure on record and 34% more than a year earlier, El Financiero reports. January–August shipments reached $419.3 billion, up 18%, giving Mexico 17.4% of all US imports, ahead of Canada at 11.2% and Taiwan at 7.7%. Tariff threats and all, Mexico is still Washington's number-one supplier.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Morena Asks Electoral Authorities to Follow the Dollars Behind the Trending Topics</u>

Morena's Mexico City chapter asked the INE and the city's electoral institute to document every form of foreign intervention ahead of the 2027 elections. "There are truckloads of millions of dollars inflating trends on social networks, wanting to buy the public conversation," said state party leader Paulo García González. The request comes days after Bolivia arrested the prosecutor investigating Fernando Cerimedo, the Argentine operative whose network reaches Mexico's PRI.

🇲🇽🩺 <u>73,000 Health Workers Sign Up for Mexico's New Neighborhood Clinics</u>

Since the call opened on September 14, 73,000 doctors, nurses and technicians have applied to staff Mexico's new Primary Health Care Clinics. The government is opening 12,750 of them across the 24 IMSS-Bienestar states starting in January 2027, each stocked with 60 basic medicines, internet and electronic medical records. They will treat patients whether or not they have social security.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>Palestine Asks Mexico to Check Its Companies Profiting From the Occupation</u>

Palestine's ambassador to Mexico, Nadya Rasheed, asked the Senate to review the value chains of Mexican corporations tied to illegal Israeli settlements. Mexican conglomerate Orbia is among 61 firms just added to the UN human rights office's list of 214 companies doing business in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem. Mexico defends international law at every forum, she said, but "what has been lacking are consequences when that law is systematically violated."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Investment in Mexico Grows at Its Fastest Pace in Two Years</u>

Mexico's gross fixed investment grew 6.0% year on year in July, according to INEGI. That is the fastest pace since July 2024 and the fourth monthly gain in a row, after a 17-month losing streak. Private investment rose 5.9%, its best figure in 30 months, and public investment grew 6.9%. Construction spending was up 6.9% and machinery and equipment 4.9%, El Financiero reports.
